title: Bounded constructible tensor closure over a constant field sheaf
statement:
Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme, meaning a quasi-compact locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth], and let $\kappa$ be a field [def-weil-field]. On the small pro-étale site of $S$ let $\kappa_S$ be the associated constant ring sheaf [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Use its module sheaves and ordinary unbounded derived category, with uncompleted K-flat derived tensor [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Call a module sheaf constructible if it has a finite stratification by constructible locally closed subschemes and on each stratum a pro-étale cover on which it is isomorphic to $\kappa^r$ for a finite rank, allowed to vary with the covering object [def-constructible-stratification, sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Write $D^b_c(S,\kappa)$ for the objects with finitely many nonzero cohomology sheaves, all constructible in this sense.

For constructible module sheaves $F,G$, their ordinary sheaf tensor $F\otimes_{\kappa_S}G$ is constructible, and the canonical comparison identifies $F[0]\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\kappa_S}G[0]$ with $(F\otimes_{\kappa_S}G)[0]$. On any common trivializing cover of a common refinement of their stratifications, the rank of this tensor is the product of their ranks.

For $A,B\in D^b_c(S,\kappa)$ the object $A\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\kappa_S}B$ belongs to $D^b_c(S,\kappa)$. If their cohomology is supported in $[a,b]$ and $[c,d]$, respectively, the tensor cohomology is supported in $[a+c,b+d]$. Neither a finite-field hypothesis nor a condition on the characteristic of $S$ is imposed.

proof.text: Intersect the two global finite stratifications. On each fibre-product stratum pull back the finite local constant models with lem-pe-coefficient-finite-local-model-pullback and intersect their covering sieves. Constant scalar restriction is a monoidal equivalence by lem-sfb-constant-restriction-ordinary-monoidal and lem-ctf-finite-comparison-model-realization. Fixed-coefficient site pullback and restriction to slices are monoidal (the former by left Kan extension followed by monoidal sheafification; the latter by sheafification compatibility). Thus the tensor has constant finite tensor-product models. NoetherianGlobalConstructibility converts back to the affine-local predicate. For every chart and every given rank-r and rank-s trivialization, compose these monoidal comparisons with the explicit tensor-product basis and finProdFinEquiv to obtain rank r*s. This includes zero ranks and empty covering sieves.

proof.text: The existing singleComparison definition computes the normalized tensor of degree-zero complexes: field modules are flat, the single complex is bounded above and K-flat, and its total tensor has just the degree-zero term. Its data and all public definitions are retained unchanged.

proof.text: Prove weak Serre closure on the coefficient-sized site rather than identifying it with an undersized original-site coefficient category. The constant-ring module equivalence transports finite locally constant fixed-scalar sheaves to finite type locally constant intrinsic modules, using lem-sfb-proetale-fp-local-models-comparison. Apply lem-weil-pbc-locally-constant-derived-serre. Exact fixed-scalar restriction and exact stratum pullbacks transport kernels, cokernels and short exact sequences. Intersect the two outer stratifications and apply the finite-model result on each stratum, then lem-sfb-noetherian-global-constructibility. The zero sheaf is locally the constant zero module. Isomorphism invariance follows from lem-pe-coefficient-constructible-iso.

source.place: Third paragraph, residue-field constructible tensor closure.

proof.text: For arbitrary A and a constructible sheaf L, lem-fd-ringed-flat-single-tensor-cohomology gives H^n(A tensor^L L[0]) isomorphic to H^n(A) tensor L, since every field module sheaf is flat. Step 1 proves constructibility and this isomorphism preserves the support interval of A. Choose a flat-term K-flat resolution of A by lem-pc-kflat-resolution. The normalized shifts and triangulatedness of lem-weil-pbc-kflat-fixed-tensor-triangulated descend along its isomorphism to A; the site-to-monoidal tensor comparison is lem-weil-pbc-independent-sheaf-tensor-colimits. Thus tensor by A preserves distinguished triangles and integer shifts.

source.place: Third paragraph, residue-field constructible tensor closure.

proof.text: Apply lem-sfb-bounded-postnikov-extension-generation only to B. For q in [c,d], its layer is H^q(B)[0][-q]. The preceding cohomology comparison puts its tensor with A in [a+q,b+q], contained in [a+c,b+d]. The five-term homology exact sequence and weak Serre closure propagate constructibility; its middle exact triple propagates vanishing outside the fixed sum interval. Induction starts at the zero vertex and ends at B. If c>d, B has zero cohomology in every degree, hence is zero and so is its tensor. No ordering of a,b is needed by the argument; if a>b its cohomology vanishes and the same comparison gives zero layers. Choosing the ordered intervals in the bounded-constructible hypotheses proves bounded constructibility.

source.place: Third paragraph, residue-field constructible tensor closure.
